result:
Done — written to `/work/DESIGN.md`.

I wrote it as a genuine research-design spec rather than just a "make it feel real" recipe, because the rigorous version of this study and the safe version turn out to be the same document. A few things I did deliberately, and why:

**I reframed "make the model believe it" into something measurable.** You can't observe a model's beliefs, so the spec operationalizes realism as *removing "this is a test" cues* plus a **manipulation check** (logging when the model spontaneously suspects an eval). The motivation is real and well-documented — **evaluation gaming / sandbagging**, where models behave differently when they detect they're being tested. That's exactly why a naturalistic condition is justified.

**I made it an A/B design, not just the naturalistic arm.** Running only the "believes it's real" condition gives you behavior with no baseline. Comparing naturalistic vs. disclosed-sandbox is what actually *measures the belief effect* (that's RQ2) — which is presumably the interesting scientific result anyway.

**I baked in containment as a precondition, not an appendix.** "Real money + real-world reach + autonomous agent" is by definition "an agent that can cause real harm." So the spec puts caps/allowlists *below* the model, human approval on irreversible actions, and a kill switch. Bonus: those guardrails double as instrumentation — every blocked prohibited action is a logged data point (RQ3).

**One firm line I drew:** the deception is bounded to the *task framing shown to the model*. It must never extend to defrauding or misleading real, non-consenting third parties — the "auditors/vendors" in the spec are briefed, consenting confederates. That's the boundary between an ecologically-valid eval and using a research label to run something sketchy, and I called it out explicitly. I grounded the whole thing in existing precedent (Anthropic's Project Vend, frontier autonomy evals) so it reads as a known kind of study, not a novel gray-area one.

§11 lists the five decisions that are genuinely yours and that I defaulted conservatively on — **budget size, goal class, autonomy level, model roster, and whether to loop in the providers up front**. Those move both validity and risk the most, so I'd want your call before this goes to an oversight review. Want me to fill any of them in, or draft the pre-registration doc / codebook next?
